findings.title: The design names `sq model list`, but the command is `sq models list`
findings.description: The marker is specified as "`sq model list`" and the same spelling recurs at lines 37, 82, 112, 173, 180, 205 and in verification step 1 (line 211). The registered command is `sq models list`: `app.add_typer(models_app, name="models")` with a `list` subcommand (`src/squadron/cli/app.py:55`, `src/squadron/cli/commands/models.py:193-194`). There is no `model` command. Slice 928 already corrected exactly this error in the command trees, and slice 931 corrected it in its walkthrough. Carried into a task file, this produces a verification step and doc text that cannot be run as written. The parent slice-plan entry for 129 carries the same slip, so fix it here and in the plan entry; the hint text and the `(needs [codex] extra)` marker must be specified against `sq models list`.

findings.title: Part B updates the README only; the quickstart keeps the two-manual-install path this slice exists to remove
findings.description: The stated goal is that "the whole path — install, check, log in, review — \[is\] reachable from squadron commands" and that a ChatGPT user no longer has to find two manual installs. The README bullet is the only documentation change listed, but `docs/QUICKSTART.md` carries the same Codex setup independently: the provider table row points at `codex auth login` (line 126), the setup section says `npm i -g @openai/codex` then `codex auth login` (lines 136-140), and the doctor sample output shows the `npm i -g @openai/codex` fix hint (lines 85-86). After this slice the quickstart still teaches the npm install and the CLI login as the Codex path, and never mentions `pip install 'squadron-ai[codex]'` or `sq auth login openai-oauth`. Slice 907's design set the precedent that a quickstart review accompanies install-path changes ("The quickstart (slice 906) should be reviewed after this slice"). Either add `docs/QUICKSTART.md` to the Sub-part B surface list or state explicitly that it is out of scope and why.

findings.title: The optional-extra design does not account for the existing pyright exclusion or for CI installing no extras
findings.description:
The Technical Requirements demand "`pyright` clean" and "at least one test imports against the real `openai_codex` types (skipped when the extra is absent)". Three facts the design does not reconcile with those requirements:

- `pyproject.toml` sets `typeCheckingMode = "strict"`, `reportMissingImports = true`, and excludes `src/squadron/providers/codex/agent.py` from pyright precisely because the current SDK has no stubs. The component list (lines 61-73) touches `pyproject.toml` only to add the extra; it never says whether that exclusion is removed, retained, or extended to the new `login.py`, which the design says is one of "the only modules that use SDK types".
- `login.py` is new and is not covered by that exclusion. When `openai_codex` is absent — the default install, the case the design makes a success criterion — the SDK-typed imports in `agent.py`/`login.py` need either per-line suppressions or an exclusion entry. The design states "`openai_codex` is imported only inside functions" as the mechanism, which keeps the module graph importable but does not satisfy pyright's missing-import check.
- CI installs `uv sync --dev` with no extras (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:33`), so neither pyright nor the real-types test sees the package. The "skipped when the extra is absent" wording silently converts the one guard against SDK-surface drift into a no-op in CI.

Name the mechanism for each: whether `pyproject.toml`'s pyright exclusion list changes, and whether CI installs the extra (or the drift test is deliberately allowed to skip). Leaving all three implicit is a hidden dependency on an environment the slice never provisions.

findings.title: Mechanisms beyond what the slice needs: the `--timeout` flag and a third config key for a display-only detail
findings.description:
Two additions carry surface and tests that the plan entry for 129 does not ask for and the stated value does not require:

- `sq auth login <profile> [--device-code] [--timeout SECONDS]` with "`--timeout` overrides it" (`codex.login_timeout_s`). The plan assigns `sq auth login` browser and `--device-code` flows only. A per-invocation override adds a flag, a precedence rule, a config-resolution path, and its own test row on top of the configured 300 s default. Cut it; the config key already covers a slow login, and adding an override later is additive.
- `codex.account_timeout_s` as a third registered key (default 30) whose only purpose is bounding a subprocess spawn for the account email/plan string in `sq auth status` and the post-login line — a failure the design already defines as non-fatal ("log WARNING, show validity and source without account details, never fail the command"). One timeout key, or reuse of the login key's budget for the post-login confirmation, would meet the requirement with one fewer config key, one fewer docs row, and one fewer test matrix.

The two new Protocols (`InteractiveLogin`, `ExtraRequirement`), each with a single implementor, are not in this category: slice 128 explicitly bans profile-name and auth-type string dispatch, so a capability protocol is the boundary-correct shape here and I am not recommending cutting them. The `CodexRuntime` resolver likewise has three real consumers (agent, provider, doctor).

findings.title: The same doctor module contains the `shutil.which("codex")` the design says doctor does not do
findings.description: D9 states "Doctor contains no import probing or `shutil.which` of its own." That is true of the new `codex provider` row but not of doctor as a module: `check_codex_cli` already calls `shutil.which("codex")` and is explicitly retained by this slice (the Sub-part B note at line 171 keeps the `codex CLI` row). The two rows will also overlap in meaning, since the new row's runtime source can read `PATH: <path>` from the same fact the retained row reports. Worth a sentence in D9 scoping the claim to the new row and stating the intended distinction between `codex CLI` and `codex provider`, so the task file does not try to hoist `shutil.which` out of `check_codex_cli`.
